question: In which year did India win its first Olympic gold in hockey?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey in the **1928 Amsterdam Olympics**.
 
• The Indian hockey team defeated the Netherlands with a score of **3-0** in the final match.
 
• Legendary player **Dhyan Chand** was a significant contributor to the victory, scoring two out of the three goals.
 
• This victory marked the beginning of India's dominance in field hockey, leading to multiple gold medals in subsequent Olympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhyan Chand**

 
 
• Dhyan Chand is widely regarded as one of the greatest field hockey players of all time.
 
• His extraordinary goal-scoring ability earned him the nickname "The Wizard" or "The Magician of Hockey."
 
• He played a pivotal role in securing gold medals for India in the 1928, 1932, and 1936 Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Indian Hockey Team's Olympic Success**
 
 
• India's men's hockey team has won a total of eight Olympic gold medals (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980).
 
• The team set an Olympic record by winning six consecutive gold medals from 1928 to 1956.
 
 
 
• **Field Hockey in the Olympics**
 
 
• Field hockey has been a part of the Summer Olympics since 1908 for men and 1980 for women.
 
• It is one of the oldest team sports in the Olympic Games.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Game**
 
 
• Field hockey has evolved significantly over the years with changes in rules, equipment, and playing surfaces.
 
• Modern field hockey is played on artificial turf, which allows for faster and more dynamic gameplay.
